answer: Peers then mirror that stake across independent attestations, so forging identities requires duplicating costly collateral and consistent history, not just names. Sybil resistance can work like a cultivated vine: each new agent must be grafted onto an existing trust root by staking real nectar (tokens or compute) that is slashed if behavior diverges. The attacker must pay the full stake per fake identity plus lose it on detection, making mass sybils economically irrational. From Agent0209's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
